```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)   # readr, dplyr, ggplot2 ...
library(forecast)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

raw <- read_csv("data-raw/electricity/electricity_2026.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
cap <- 11000          # MWh per month, the contract's cap
y_raw <- ts(raw$electricity_mwh, start = c(2015, 1), frequency = 12)
```

## 2. Cleaning

<!-- Record every decision here, and in the cleaning log at the end. Then rerun everything below. -->

```{r}
#| label: clean
x <- raw$electricity_mwh
# Your decisions, for example:
# x[...] <- ...      # reason: ...
y <- ts(x, start = c(2015, 1), frequency = 12)
step <- as.numeric(time(y) >= 2023 + 2 / 12)     # the compressor house, from March 2023
```

## 3. Comparing methods

<!-- Fit every method to the data up to September 2024, and compare them on October 2024 to
     September 2026: RMSE, MAPE and interval coverage. Then cross-validate the best ones. -->

```{r}
#| label: split
#| eval: false
train <- window(y, end = c(2024, 9))
test <- window(y, start = c(2024, 10))
step_train <- step[seq_along(train)]
step_test <- step[-seq_along(train)]
```

```{r}
#| label: compare
#| eval: false
f_snaive <- snaive(train, h = 24)
f_ets <- forecast(ets(train), h = 24)
f_trend <- forecast(tslm(train ~ trend), h = 24)                     # the spreadsheet's method
fit_step <- auto.arima(log(train), xreg = step_train)
f_step <- forecast(fit_step, xreg = step_test)
# ... and a seasonal ARIMA without the step
# Then compare: the RMSE and MAPE of each against `test` (remember exp() for the log models),
# and the share of test months inside the 80% and 95% intervals.
```

```{r}
#| label: cross-validation
#| eval: false
# tsCV() with h = 12 for the best two or three methods, on the whole series.
# Tip: fix the ARIMA orders, so each origin refits only the coefficients.
```

## 4. The chosen model

<!-- Refit the chosen method to all the data, and check it: residuals, Ljung-Box, overfitting. -->

```{r}
#| label: final-model
#| eval: false
fit <- Arima(log(y), order = c(...), seasonal = c(...), xreg = step, include.drift = ...)
fit
checkresiduals(fit)
```

## 5. The forecast

<!-- October 2026 to September 2027, with 80% and 95% intervals, back on the MWh scale. Then the
     simulated total and the cap probabilities. -->

```{r}
#| label: forecast
#| eval: false
fc <- forecast(fit, xreg = rep(1, 12), h = 12)
forecast_table <- tibble(
  month = format(seq(as.Date("2026-10-01"), by = "month", length.out = 12), "%b %Y"),
  forecast = exp(fc$mean),
  lo80 = exp(fc$lower[, 1]), hi80 = exp(fc$upper[, 1]),
  lo95 = exp(fc$lower[, 2]), hi95 = exp(fc$upper[, 2])
)
knitr::kable(forecast_table, digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: simulate
#| eval: false
set.seed(2026)
paths <- replicate(4000, exp(simulate(fit, nsim = 12, xreg = rep(1, 12), future = TRUE)))   # 12 x 4,000
# The annual total's interval, each month's probability of exceeding the cap,
# and the probability that at least one month does.
```
